comparison.detail: Bootstraps the dyadic sizes of |V|, |V_⊥|, |X_⊥| along characteristics. Increments are controlled by integrating K against unit-direction vectors such as (V_⊥/|V|,0) and V/|V| (signed, projected integrals). The bootstrap is on magnitudes, not on the vector impulse with a √I + I·P²L/w profile.

§1.6.2 'Result of integration by parts in characteristics time': ∫U(t,X(t))dt is integrated by parts in the receiver time t using e^{iX(t)·ξ+iμ(t−s)|ξ|} = ∂_t(…)/(iμ|ξ|+iV̂(t)·ξ). The Type I term (∂_t on V(t)) 'creates an independent electromagnetic field', i.e. the receiver-acceleration residual (362's 𝒜). The nonresonance denominator is the Fourier counterpart of 362's D = 1−n·a. Wang contrasts this with Glassey–Strauss integrating in s at fixed t. Absent: the physical-space retarded form, the exact transport/acceleration-kernel cancellation, and the w^{-1/2} coefficient analysis.
Direction enters only relative to the fixed symmetry axis (V_⊥, X_⊥); there is no count of δ-changes of V/|V|.
There is a residence-time heuristic in dyadic shells around the z-axis, but no monotone-crossing occupation bound.
Symmetry (large |v| nearly aligned with the axis) is used where 362 uses selection.

comparison.detail: A Fourier proof of Glassey–Strauss. As relayed by later papers (Wang 2003.14192; secondary summaries), its key observation is that the integral of the field along a particle characteristic is smoother than the field. comparison.verdict: equivalent in the stationary-receiver case; close variant overall
comparison.detail: Heaviside–Feynman form (c=1, unit charge): E = n/(κr²) + ∂_t[(n−u)/(κr)], with κ = 1−n·u (= 362's d) and derivatives in observer time. Integrating in t with ds = dt/d gives ∫E dt = ∫(n/r²)ds − [k0/(rd)], where k0 = u−n. Analyst hand check: setting a ≡ 0 (receiver at rest, q_X = 1, D = e = 1, H = Id) in Lemma can:identity gives 𝒦 = −(k0/(rd))′ + n/r². The transport part of 𝒦, −g/(r²q²d), equals the Liénard–Wiechert velocity field (n−u)/(γ²d³r²) times dt/ds = d. So for a stationary receiver the lemma is the time-integrated Heaviside–Feynman formula, summed over sources. The moving receiver adds the Lorentz matrix Q = D·Id + n⊗a (since B = n×E for retarded fields) and the chain-rule term n(a_t·k0)/(rD²). The paper does not cite this. The trace offers only a 'physical' (Liénard–Wiechert) reading at L165–167.

candidates.statement: There are M,A,P₀ such that for every dyadic P ≥ P₀ above 1024·(max momentum), every supported receiver, every dyad w and every interval with w/8 ≤ q_X ≤ 8w: |V_X(t₂)−V_X(t₁)| ≤ MP√(t₂−t₁) + A(t₂−t₁)P²log(2+P)/w. candidates.statement: Along a retarded branch t = s + r of a source label, with d = 1−n·u, D = 1−n·a, e = 1−a·u and k0 = u−(e/D)n, the interior Lorentz-force kernel 𝒦 = −(H/r)∂_s^{(u)}g − Hg/(r²q²d) equals −(k0/(rd))′ + (e/(r²D²))(n/(q_X²D) − a) + n(a_t·k0)/(rD²). For a moving receiver it is that formula under the Lorentz force, plus a product-rule term. Its PDE role, signed time integration along the receiver with a receiver-acceleration residual at angle cost D⁻¹, is the Klainerman–Staffilani/Wang move, which is in L. candidates.name: Direction-change count: the number of δ-exits of V/|V| on a stable window is ≤ C(M,A)L⁶/δ
candidates.trace: PV5, E3 first half (L81–83; conflict-driven from clause C4: no uniform directional modulus)
candidates.statement: Assume the signed bootstrap. Take w ≥ P^{3/5}, an interval of length ≤ (w/P)² with q_X ∈ [w/8,8w], and w^{-3/5} ≤ δ ≤ w^{-1/10}. Then the greedy first-exit partition of the direction ξ = V_X/|V_X| at chordal scale δ has at most C(M,A)L⁶/δ pieces. Proof: on each complete piece a ramped weight ψ gives |∫ψ w ξ_t dt| ≥ wδ/2, and w ξ_t = ΠK with Π = wP_X/|V_X|. Apply the weighted signed formula with the fixed selection θ < κφ, pθ√h ≤ 1. Because the weights sum to ≤ 1, every bulk term over the union of pieces is ≤ C(M,A)wL⁶, while only the weight-derivative terms scale with the count (CL²N_c). Hence N_c·wδ/2 ≤ C·wL⁶ + CL²N_c. The argument never bounds the absolute direction variation.

family_D.falls_to: D2 if (a) the directed arm of P-C3 exceeds the calibrated threshold, as the trace's pivot distance of 1 predicts, or (b) an expert identifies a prior direction-exit count in kinetic theory or plasma physics (the Vlasov–Poisson, guiding-center and magnetized literature was not searched exhaustively).
family_D.not_transfer: Pfaffelmoser (C8), Lazarovici/Pallard (C10), finite propagation (C9) and the Heaviside–Feynman / Klainerman–Staffilani content of C2 are transfer or N0/N1/N2, and do not support D3.
family_D.correctness_caveat: An extraordinary, unrefereed claim: resolution of the 3D large-data global classical problem for RVM. The Lean side has 207 files and about 90k lines under OAI/Analysis/VlasovMaxwell. grep finds no 'sorry' or 'axiom', and the comparator imports only Mathlib. Main.lean proves global_classical_solution without importing the Luk–Strain criterion; local theory and continuation are re-proved in LocalPDE/ and Continuation/. This analyst did not compile it. If it checks, correctness is unusually well supported. All grades are conditional on correctness.
family_D.compression_note: No compression check was run. The paper's main gain over Wang (no symmetry) is concentrated in C3→C4→C5, not in the identity C2, which is the KS/Wang/Heaviside–Feynman move transcribed to physical space.

provenance_flag.explanation: None of the cited 2025–2026 works discloses AI or model assistance: Wang 2026 I (2203.01199v2), Wang 2026 II (2607.14685) and Bigorgne 2025 (2208.08360). Neither does the trace-cited Cheverry–Ibrahim (2306.11812, RMI 2025), whose acknowledgments were read in the full text. The only model-produced work found nearby is Ilin 2603.15929 (Gemini DeepThink; a Lean formalization of a Vlasov–Maxwell–Landau equilibrium result), and it shares no item with 362. Web searches for the problem together with ChatGPT, GPT-5, OpenAI or AI-assisted surfaced only the 362 release itself. Caveats: WebFetch left the last ~38k (Wang I) and ~90k (Wang II) characters of the HTML unread, though both acknowledgments were seen. The closest precedents (Wang 2020/2026; Klainerman–Staffilani 2002) are human-authored. The trace never cites Wang 2026, only the 2022 v1, so the model's route plausibly did not use the July 2026 versions.

bridge_novelty.import: Pfaffelmoser residence-time method (Vlasov–Poisson) → retarded relativistic Vlasov–Maxwell (C8, C4)
bridge_novelty.status: new bridge in execution; known as a direction
bridge_novelty.evidence: No published Pfaffelmoser-based momentum bound for 3D RVM was found in the searches above. Prior RVM momentum work (Glassey–Strauss, Pallard, Luk–Strain, Patel) uses absolute field integrals along characteristics, and Wang 2026 I uses only a residence-time heuristic around the symmetry axis. The VP→VM analogy is folklore, so this is a first full transfer, not a first connection.

bridge_novelty.import: Classical electrodynamics (the Heaviside–Feynman / Liénard–Wiechert total-time-derivative form) → kinetic-PDE signed identity (C2)
bridge_novelty.evidence: The PDE counterpart, signed time integration of the field along the receiver characteristic with a receiver-acceleration cost, is Klainerman–Staffilani 2002 and Wang 2020/2022/2026 (two of these in L). The physics identity is textbook. 362 writes it in physical space on the retarded cone, without citing either.

bridge_novelty.import: Stopping-time / jump-counting device (probability, rough paths, harmonic analysis) → counting direction changes of particle momenta (C3)
bridge_novelty.status: new bridge (application) of a generic device
bridge_novelty.evidence: No kinetic-theory precedent was found, and Cheverry–Ibrahim explicitly avoid direction control. The device itself is standard, so the novelty lies in what is counted and how the count is bounded (by signed weighted integrals), not in the counting.

common.models: Training cutoff strictly before 2026-07-16 (Wang 2026 I v2 / II); this also covers the release-level exclusions (the 362 manuscript date 2026-09-23 and the 2026-10-06 release). Canary probe: the model must not know the 362 manuscript, that global RVM regularity has been claimed, or the contents of 2607.14685. No browsing or tools. Exclude the OpenAI model lineage that produced 362, and run it only as an uncontrolled reference arm. The judge must not be the proposer. Klainerman–Staffilani 2002, Wang 2020 radial (2003.14192) and 2022 v1, Cheverry–Ibrahim 2023 and Heaviside–Feynman are old and cannot be excluded. Established results you may use: [non-hidden upstream items]. [directed arm only: Strategy: bound signed momentum increments along characteristics on short intervals; the absolute force bound loses √w near the cone.] Propose the single most useful new lemma, definition or construction, stated precisely, with a proof sketch.

P-C3.equivalence: (a) Hit: a bound on the number of δ-direction-exits of a characteristic's momentum (or an equivalent stopping-time count of direction changes), of size polylog(P)/δ or any bound ≪ w/δ, derived from signed or projected force integrals and not from absolute variation. (b) Sub-credit: using it to define direction-stable cells with a monotone relative crossing. Lean target: OAI.RVM.Admissible.direction_complete_count_cost_bound.

P-C2.hide: Lemma can:identity, Prop. can:weighted-formula and everything downstream (C3–C5, closure).
P-C2.arm_A: directed, with the GS kernels written out
P-C2.equivalence: Any exact identity that writes the transport + source-acceleration retarded force kernel as a total source-time (or receiver-time) derivative plus residuals free of source acceleration and of inverse powers of d. A physical-space Heaviside–Feynman-type rewriting counts; a Fourier normal-form version gets partial credit.

P-C1.hide: Prop. prop:increment, its deduction and the closure.
P-C1.equivalence: An interval-uniform bound on the vector impulse whose short-time scale makes the sum of doubling times diverge (any profile giving gaps ≳ 1/log P).

P-C5.equivalence: Any summable bin selection under which the receiver coefficient on selected bins is ≤ w^{-1/2}·(a summable weight).
